description: Matched (nginx + ngx_pagespeed) Linux binaries for WeAmp.PageSpeed.Sidecar. Reference this alongside WeAmp.PageSpeed.Sidecar to supply the bundled reverse-proxy engine for linux-x64 / linux-arm64.
releaseNotes:
1.17.0 (engine v1.17.0, bundled nginx 1.30.4): the package follows the mod_pagespeed 1.17.0 release and is licensed under the Apache License 2.0; LICENSE and NOTICE ship in the package. Licensing is removed from the package and from the bundled module: the retired licensing settings are accepted and ignored, so existing appsettings configuration keeps working (setting them in code now raises an obsolete-member warning). Security: the bundled nginx moves from 1.30.3 to 1.30.4 (CVE-2026-42533), and the native engine carries the 1.17.0 security fixes, among them a denial-of-service fix in the nginx module, cache-integrity and information-disclosure fixes for in-place optimization, request-forgery hardening of the admin console, and the bundled HTTPS fetch library updated to curl 8.22.0; update recommended. Reliability: a worker process that starts at an unlucky moment no longer hangs, and a process that dies while holding a shared-memory lock no longer hangs the others. After updating, if you set Cache.FileCachePath or Sidecar.ConfigDirectory (so the disk cache persists across restarts): the disk cache moves to a new format and starts empty once; also flush it once (touch cache.flush in the cache directory) so entries recorded by earlier releases are dropped. With the default per-process cache location there is nothing to do. Full notes: https://modpagespeed.com/docs/release-notes/#v1-17-0

1.15.0.7 (packaging revision; engine v1.15.0+r18, bundled nginx 1.30.3): native-engine refresh from r17 to r18. Serving performance: cached resources are served with substantially less copying, including an experimental zero-copy serve mode for memory-mapped cache hits, and HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 cached serves stream through a bounded copy ring. Caching: metadata and page-property entries move to a dedicated small-object tier so they stay warm across restarts independent of payload traffic (on file caches of ~256 MB or larger the first restart after upgrading rebuilds the payload cache once; set FileCacheSmallTierPercent 0 to disable), and the default file cache size is raised to 1 GB. Correctness: stricter configuration validation (out-of-range option values now fail configuration load, and an invalid ?PageSpeedFilters= name consistently rejects the query), critical-CSS and Content-Security-Policy fixes (script-injecting filters back off under a restrictive policy when HonorCsp is enabled), a native loading="lazy" mode for lazyload_images, and the legacy JavaScript minifier now passes template literals through unmodified. Security hardening across input validation and output escaping, an updated bundled HTTPS fetch library (curl 8.21.0), and cache-library fixes including a concurrent-startup initialization race; update recommended. The embedded admin console also gets a reliability and usability pass. No change to the bundled nginx (still 1.30.3) and no managed-code changes; 1.15.0 installs keep working.

1.15.0.6 (packaging revision; engine v1.15.0+r17, bundled nginx 1.30.3): security fix in the bundled nginx module — a malformed request could crash an nginx worker process (remotely triggerable denial of service, no authentication required); update strongly recommended. Optimization and page-property caches now persist across restarts, so the server comes back warm after a restart or deploy instead of re-optimizing from scratch. Also includes the engine's experimental, default-off Web Bot Auth updates (real-world signer interop and the opt-in AI-crawl counter). No change to the bundled nginx (still 1.30.3) and no managed-code changes; 1.15.0 installs keep working.

1.15.0.5 (packaging revision; engine v1.15.0+r16, bundled nginx 1.30.3): security-maintenance update to the bundled reverse proxy. The bundled nginx moves from 1.30.2 to 1.30.3 on the 1.30 stable branch, picking up upstream fixes for a buffer-overflow issue in nginx's upstream proxy/gRPC handling (CVE-2026-42055) and a lower-severity charset buffer-overread (CVE-2026-48142); update recommended. No change to optimization behavior and no managed-code changes — the native engine is unchanged (v1.15.0+r16). 1.15.0 installs keep working.

1.15.0.4 (packaging revision; engine v1.15.0+r16, bundled nginx 1.30.2): native-engine refresh from r15 to r16, with no change to optimization behavior or bundled nginx (still 1.30.2). This build picks up minor engine correctness and shutdown-path hardening from r16. No managed-code changes; 1.15.0 installs keep working.

1.15.0.3 (packaging revision; engine v1.15.0+r15, bundled nginx 1.30.2): native-engine refresh from r10 to r15 — a security-maintenance update to the bundled module, with no change to optimization behavior or bundled nginx (still 1.30.2). The shipped .so is now built with binary hardening (full RELRO/BIND_NOW, -fstack-protector-strong, _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2, and CET/BTI), asserted on every release artifact. The rewrite path picks up memory-safety and resource-exhaustion fixes, along with explicit bounds on header count and HTML nesting depth; update recommended. The module's attack surface is further reduced by removing unused third-party components and updating the remaining vendored dependencies to maintained versions. No managed-code changes; 1.15.0 installs keep working.

1.15.0.2 (packaging revision; engine v1.15.0+r10, bundled nginx 1.30.2): NuGet packaging refresh on the same native engine as 1.15.0.1.

1.15.0.1 (packaging revision; engine v1.15.0+r10, bundled nginx 1.30.2): refreshed embedded admin console. The native engine also picks up the runtime ABI guard (inert for the bundled matched pair; relevant only in External mode against a drifted host nginx). No managed-code changes; 1.15.0 installs keep working.

1.15.0 (GA): the Inverse topology is the default. Add services.AddPageSpeed(config) + app.UsePageSpeed() to your ASP.NET Core app and your Kestrel server stays the public front door — it owns the listening socket, TLS, auth and routing exactly as before. The bundled nginx + ngx_pagespeed runs loopback-only behind your app as an optimize-proxy: the middleware streams optimizable responses over loopback (YARP) to nginx, which optimizes and proxy_pass-es back to a private raw-origin Kestrel endpoint where the middleware bypasses itself. Non-optimizable requests, and any request while the sidecar isn't running, pass straight through un-optimized (always-functional). By default (Sidecar.OwnPublicPort = true) the package binds the public port (Sidecar.ListenPort, 8080) as a code endpoint; set OwnPublicPort = false to bind it yourself via Kestrel:Endpoints (e.g. for in-process TLS). For edge TLS, front the public port with a terminator or load balancer; the loopback hop to nginx is plain HTTP with a single validated X-Forwarded-Proto so optimized asset URLs root at the public scheme.

Zero-config host handling (forward-all): optimization works for any host your app serves with no domain configuration, because the module implicitly authorizes each request's own same-origin resources. Domains.AuthorizedDomains is not a setup step; localhost is always optimized. Defense-in-depth: set Sidecar.RestrictToAuthorizedHosts = true to optimize only hosts you list. The /pagespeed_* admin endpoints return 404 from the public front door by default; set Sidecar.AllowPublicAdmin = true (requires AdminAuth.Enabled) to expose them behind the bearer token.

Modes: Inverse (default), Process (the classic front-proxy where nginx is the public front door — still supported), and External (operator-managed nginx). Docker is reserved and fails validation.

The bundled nginx is on the 1.30 stable branch (1.30.3). A native pagespeed-nginx-launch shim, on by default (Sidecar.UseLaunchShim), arms PR_SET_PDEATHSIG so the bundled nginx can't be orphaned (and hold its loopback port) if the host process is hard-killed (SIGKILL/OOM/container hard-stop) once launch has settled; the bundled runtime identifier (RID) is derived at runtime so the matched nginx resolves on linux-arm64 as well as linux-x64; and a per-RID build-info.json provenance manifest is emitted. The native engine targets a glibc 2.31 floor with statically-linked libstdc++ and no OpenSSL host dependency, so it loads on Debian 11/12, Ubuntu 20.04+, RHEL/Alma 9 and Amazon Linux 2023. A single dotnet add package auto-pulls the native engine; binaries are stripped (debug archived separately). This package is mod_pagespeed 1.15 (jpeg/png/webp recompression, CSS/JS minification, critical-CSS inlining, Core-Web-Vitals HTML rewriting), and the bundled nginx module transcodes AVIF through opt-in filters.
title: WeAmp.PageSpeed.Sidecar Native Binaries — Linux (x64, arm64)
